part1.teacher: Sort six animal cards using one visible feature, modelling opposite group labels. Ask each pair to explain a placement and photograph or record their completed groups.
part1.pupils: Sort and label six cards; explain the selected feature using one animal.

part2.teacher: Ask pupils to reconstruct the rule using two of their saved cards, then test a second visible feature on the same set.
part2.pupils: Re-sort the cards by a different feature and explain why a card changes groups.

L02.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Use tomato growth cards to model the sequence from seed to germination. Guide groups to place the young plant, flowering and fruiting cards and identify a visible clue.
part1.pupils: Order all five cards and annotate a clue for each neighbouring pair.

part2.teacher: Revisit the group's completed tomato sequence and ask pupils to explain the transition from flowering to fruiting.
part2.pupils: Point to the changes in two neighbouring stages and prepare to order the new okra cards independently.

L24.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Use a safe dry-cell kit with an open switch. Present a single fault at a time and model predicting where the circuit is incomplete before checking. Open the switch before handling components.
part1.pupils: Predict and check faults in the low-voltage kit; record the observed result for each safe test.

part2.teacher: Present a different incomplete circuit diagram; ask pupils to use their earlier records to choose the first point to check.
part2.pupils: Mark the suspected break, explain the prediction and check the proposed correction using the teacher's diagram.

L36.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Use picture cards to model food being broken into smaller components and locate the process in the digestive system. Build a class sequence without real food.
part1.pupils: Order the picture cards and explain what changes at each stage.

part2.teacher: Revisit the sequence and use a nutrient card to connect smaller components to the body's use of nutrients.
part2.pupils: Explain the link between breaking food down and the body using nutrients before completing the individual explanation.

L18.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Model a two-step cause-and-effect chain showing new plants replacing old plants. Give groups food, shelter and survival context cards.
part1.pupils: Arrange arrows to show the replacement of plants and identify one organism that depends on them.

part2.teacher: Ask pupils to revisit their arrows and predict the result if the supply of new plants stops.
part2.pupils: Explain the predicted consequence using the chosen context, then prepare an individual cause-and-effect diagram.

L26.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Model packing a full layer of unit cubes in a box without gaps. Guide pairs to count the first layer and fill remaining layers.
part1.pupils: Pack the cubes, record the number in each layer and calculate the total.

part2.teacher: Review the saved layer counts and check an example with a missing cube. Model recording the total in cm³.
part2.pupils: Correct the example and explain why each layer must be complete before independently measuring a small box.

L32.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Prepare area and volume stations. Demonstrate a suitable tool and a technique for each; supervise pupils measuring at both stations.
part1.pupils: Measure or check one area and one volume, and record the results with units.

part2.teacher: Ask pairs to compare their recorded values and explain why the chosen tool and unit match each measurement.
part2.pupils: Check both units and rehearse one evidence-based reason for a tool or method choice before individual assessment.

L35.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Show a potato piece in fresh water and provide a pretested salt solution. Help groups plan two trials, keeping the object and liquid amount similar.
part1.pupils: Test the same piece in both liquids and record whether it floats or sinks.

part2.teacher: Revisit the two trial records and ask what changed when salt dissolved. Compare the same piece in both liquids.
part2.pupils: Use the observations to explain how the denser salt solution changed the outcome.

L38.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Compare documented descriptions of familiar acidic and alkaline examples with separate litmus records. Explain safe evidence sources and do not allow tasting or touching unknown liquids.
part1.pupils: Use the cards to compare examples, separating description evidence from indicator-colour evidence.

part2.teacher: Present an unlabelled-liquid scenario and ask pupils to select a safe evidence source.
part2.pupils: Explain why an unknown sample must be referred to the teacher and use the documented indicator results for comparison.

L41.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

part1.teacher: Use a checked chart of four planets' revolution periods in consistent units. Model ordering one pair and guide groups to order all four.
part1.pupils: Arrange the four planets by period and record each value with its unit.

part2.teacher: Provide the distance row from the same chart; ask pupils to compare the two ordered sets.
part2.pupils: Identify the distance–period pattern supported by the chart before completing the individual task.

L47.structure: Part 1: original induction, guided main activity and evidence checkpoint. Part 2: recap/continuation, original independent assessment and closure.

32.teacher: Give pupils a new set of opaque, translucent and transparent materials. Hold torch, screen and material positions constant.
32.pupils: Observe each shadow, record its clarity and justify the comparison using the three results.

35.teacher: Supply low-voltage component trays and two circuit drawings in different layouts. Ask pupils to locate the same components without connecting to mains electricity.
35.pupils: Match and label cells, bulbs and switches in each layout; distinguish each component from its holder or connecting wire.

42.teacher: Provide a working low-voltage tester and safe samples of metal, wood and plastic; check the tester first.
42.pupils: Predict, test and classify the samples; record evidence for whether each allows current through the tester.

48.teacher: Provide two teacher-prepared safe-temperature water samples and equal sugar portions; keep the amounts and stirring identical.
48.pupils: Time the disappearance of visible grains, compare the two readings and identify temperature as the changed factor.

50.teacher: Use equal amounts of salt and water at the same temperature; stir one cup steadily while leaving the other still.
50.pupils: Record visible grains at agreed intervals, compare the cups and explain the effect of stirring.

57.teacher: Provide a prepared covered bowl with droplets under the cooled cover and a labelled water-cycle picture.
57.pupils: Sketch the droplets' path, compare the model to cloud formation and rain, and explain what the cooled cover represents.

59.teacher: Provide an air-mixture diagram with oxygen and carbon dioxide labels removed and a separate set of gas cards.
59.pupils: Place the labels, explain why air is a mixture and identify the gas needed for breathing.

63.teacher: Show a teacher demonstration of air escaping from a tilted submerged cup and a paper sail moving in moving air.
63.pupils: Record one observation from each demonstration and explain what each shows about air.

69.teacher: Provide a completed model and a comparison photograph showing one support removed. Ask pupils to inspect the parts safely.
69.pupils: Record two visible features and explain how the support helps the model stand or function.

1.teacher: Provide three safe objects at sight, touch and listening stations with a mix of observations and guesses on cards.
1.pupils: Record one evidence statement at each station, identify the sense used and correct one unsupported guess.

8.teacher: Provide a magnifier, blunt tongs, labelled trays and a safe specimen transfer path.
8.pupils: Inspect and transfer the specimen carefully, demonstrate correct tool handling and explain one precaution.

11.teacher: Give pupils unfamiliar tooth diagrams and illustrated cutting, tearing and grinding actions.
11.pupils: Match incisors, canines and molars to the functions; explain one match from the visible tooth shape.

14.teacher: Provide textbook diagrams of milk and permanent teeth with labels concealed.
14.pupils: Count and compare the two sets, record the findings in a two-column table and explain which set replaces the other.

26.teacher: Provide six new illustrated animal cases with reliable diet evidence.
26.pupils: Classify the animals as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores and support two decisions using their food records.

28.teacher: Give a food log for an unfamiliar animal across several days, including plant and animal food evidence.
28.pupils: Highlight the relevant foods, infer the diet group and justify the classification from the complete log.

30.teacher: Give pairs labelled diet cards and tooth diagrams with visible broad and pointed surfaces.
30.pupils: Compare the surfaces and explain how one observed feature is associated with the food eaten.

32.teacher: Provide a short animal feeding record that includes its usual diet and a reported change in feeding behaviour.
32.pupils: Prepare a report naming the usual diet group, one supporting observation and a possible reason for the reported change.

68.teacher: Provide illustrated examples of a flagpole, well and a device without a pulley.
68.pupils: Identify rope, wheel and load where present; explain one practical benefit of using the pulley.
